audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Samuel 10, first-pass restored draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for anointing and kiss, sign sequence, prophetic-band altered state, identity-change language, Gilgal waiting instruction, private secrecy, public lot, hiding among baggage, height rhetoric, acclamation, royal custom, dissent, and mental-health/leader-cult safeguards.

verses.restored: Samuel took flask of oil, poured it upon Saul's head, kissed him, and said, Has not YHWH anointed you as leader over his inheritance?

familiar.text: Then Samuel took a vial of oil, and poured it upon his head, and kissed him, and said, Is it not because the LORD hath anointed thee to be captain over his inheritance?

verses.restored: When you go from me today, you will find two men by Rachel's tomb in border of Benjamin at Zelzah. They will say to you, Donkeys you went to seek are found, and look, your father has left matter of donkeys and is anxious for you, saying, What shall I do about my son?

familiar.text: When thou art departed from me to day, then thou shalt find two men by Rachel’s sepulchre in the border of Benjamin at Zelzah; and they will say unto thee, The asses which thou wentest to seek are found: and, lo, thy father hath left the care of the asses, and sorroweth for you, saying, What shall I do for my son?

verses.restored: You shall pass on from there and come to oak of Tabor. Three men going up to Divine at Bethel will meet you, one carrying three young goats, one carrying three loaves of bread, and one carrying a skin of wine.

familiar.text: Then shalt thou go on forward from thence, and thou shalt come to the plain of Tabor, and there shall meet thee three men going up to God to Bethel, one carrying three kids, and another carrying three loaves of bread, and another carrying a bottle of wine:

verses.restored: They will ask about your well-being and give you two loaves of bread, and you shall take them from their hand.

familiar.text: And they will salute thee, and give thee two loaves of bread; which thou shalt receive of their hands.

verses.restored: Afterward you shall come to hill of Divine where Philistine garrison is. As you come there to city, you will meet a band of prophets coming down from high place, with harp, tambourine, flute, and lyre before them, and they will be prophesying.

verses.restored: Spirit of YHWH will rush upon you, and you will prophesy with them and be turned into another man.

familiar.text: And the Spirit of the LORD will come upon thee, and thou shalt prophesy with them, and shalt be turned into another man.

verses.restored: When these signs come to you, do for yourself what your hand finds, for Divine is with you.

familiar.text: And let it be, when these signs are come unto thee, that thou do as occasion serve thee; for God is with thee.

verses.restored: You shall go down before me to Gilgal, and look, I will come down to you to offer ascending offerings and sacrifice peace offerings. Seven days you shall wait until I come to you and make known to you what you shall do.

familiar.text: And thou shalt go down before me to Gilgal; and, behold, I will come down unto thee, to offer burnt offerings, and to sacrifice sacrifices of peace offerings: seven days shalt thou tarry, till I come to thee, and shew thee what thou shalt do.

verses.restored: It happened as he turned his shoulder to go from Samuel, Divine turned for him another heart, and all these signs came that day.

familiar.text: And it was so, that when he had turned his back to go from Samuel, God gave him another heart: and all those signs came to pass that day.

verses.restored: They came there to hill, and look, a band of prophets met him. Spirit of Divine rushed upon him, and he prophesied among them.

familiar.text: And when they came thither to the hill, behold, a company of prophets met him; and the Spirit of God came upon him, and he prophesied among them.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when all that knew him beforetime saw that, behold, he prophesied among the prophets, then the people said one to another, What is this that is come unto the son of Kish? Is Saul also among the prophets?

verses.restored: A man from there answered and said, And who is their father? Therefore it became a proverb, Is Saul also among prophets?

familiar.text: And one of the same place answered and said, But who is their father? Therefore it became a proverb, Is Saul also among the prophets?

verses.restored: When he finished prophesying, he came to high place.

familiar.text: And when he had made an end of prophesying, he came to the high place.

familiar.text: And Saul’s uncle said unto him and to his servant, Whither went ye? And he said, To seek the asses: and when we saw that they were no where, we came to Samuel.

verses.restored: Saul's uncle said, Tell me, please, what Samuel said to you.

familiar.text: And Saul’s uncle said, Tell me, I pray thee, what Samuel said unto you.

familiar.text: And Saul said unto his uncle, He told us plainly that the asses were found. But of the matter of the kingdom, whereof Samuel spake, he told him not.

translation_notes: The private anointing, public lot, prophetic experience, and popular acclamation are distinct legitimating scenes; none removes the need for accountability.
Samuel's kiss is an ancient greeting/commission gesture, not permission for leaders to cross bodily boundaries.
Prophetic music and altered behavior are communal religious phenomena, not diagnostic evidence of mental illness or automatic proof of holiness.
'Turned into another man' and 'another heart' describe vocational transformation; they must not erase identity, consent, or responsibility.
The instruction to do what the hand finds is limited by the surrounding commission and cannot authorize impulsive or violent behavior.
Saul hides among baggage. Fear, reluctance, overwhelm, or privacy do not disqualify a person or prove false humility.
Public selection by lot reflects ancient discernment and cannot replace transparent, participatory governance.
Saul's height again attracts attention; bodily traits are not leadership qualifications.
'Let the king live' is political acclamation, not worship.
The 'judgment/custom of kingship' should be read beside chapter 8's warning about royal extraction.
The dissenters' insult does not justify suppression, retaliation, or compulsory gifts; Saul's silence initially restrains escalation.
safety_note: Do not use anointing, prophecy, altered states, lots, bodily appearance, crowd acclaim, or claims that Divine touched supporters' hearts to demand political obedience. Do not stigmatize Saul's hiding or prophetic behavior as mental illness. Dissent is not treason, and leaders may not punish people for withholding praise or gifts.
